doc.doc:
A CommonMark parser and HTML renderer, with optional GitHub Flavored Markdown, and the features a documentation site needs: - {@linkcode parse} turns Markdown into a syntax tree shaped like {@link https://github.com/syntax-tree/mdast | mdast}, and gives every heading a unique, GitHub-compatible `id` ({@linkcode slug} is the default algorithm; the `slugger` option replaces it). - {@linkcode render} turns that tree into HTML, with options to rewrite link and image URLs (`rewriteLink`), highlight code blocks (`highlight`), allow, escape or strip raw HTML (`html`), and leave out heading ids (`headingIds`). - {@linkcode toc} lists the headings for a table of contents. - {@linkcode visit} walks the tree, for changes between parsing and rendering. - With the `gfm` option: tables, task lists, strikethrough, extended autolinks, footnotes, and GitHub's alerts (`> [!NOTE]`) as `admonition` nodes. The parser is a port of {@link https://github.com/commonmark/commonmark.js | commonmark.js}, the CommonMark reference implementation, and passes every example in the {@link https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/ | CommonMark Spec 0.31.2}. ```ts import { parse, render } from "@ende/markdown"; import { assertEquals } from "@ende/assert"; const ast = parse("Hello, *Ende*!"); assertEquals(render(ast), "

Hello, Ende!

\n"); ``` ## Building a documentation page With {@link https://jsr.io/@ende/front-matter | @ende/front-matter} for the front matter: ```ts import { extract } from "@ende/front-matter/yaml"; import { parse, render, toc } from "@ende/markdown"; import { assertEquals } from "@ende/assert"; const source = "---\ntitle: Guide\n---\n# Guide\n\n> [!NOTE]\n> See [setup](setup.md).\n\n## Install\n\n~~~sh\nende install\n~~~\n"; // A real highlighter would add markup to the escaped code. const highlight = (code: string, lang: string | null) => lang === "sh" ? `${code}` : undefined; const { attrs, body } = extract<{ title: string }>(source); const ast = parse(body, { gfm: true }); const html = render(ast, { highlight, rewriteLink: href => href.replace(/\.md$/, "/") }); const outline = toc(ast, { maxDepth: 3 }); assertEquals(attrs.title, "Guide"); assertEquals(outline, [ { depth: 1, text: "Guide", slug: "guide" }, { depth: 2, text: "Install", slug: "install" } ]); assertEquals( html, `

Guide

Note

See setup.

Install

ende install
` ); ``` ## Heading ids Heading ids are the one way the default output differs from the HTML of the CommonMark and GFM specs: `render()` writes `

` where the specs have `

`. Pass `headingIds: false` for spec output. The default {@linkcode slug} follows GitHub (github-slugger), so `#install` links work both on GitHub and on a site built with this package, and repeated headings get `-1`, `-2` and so on. `render()` never writes an id twice: when a footnote's id (`fn-1`, `fnref-1`) is already a heading's, the footnote's id gets a suffix instead. ## Differences from mdast - Link reference definitions are resolved at parse time. A reference link such as `[text][label]` becomes a `link` node with the definition's `url` and `title`, and an image reference becomes an `image` node. The tree has no `definition`, `linkReference` or `imageReference` nodes. - Nodes have no `position` information. - Headings have an `id`, and GitHub alerts are `admonition` nodes. - A `code` node's `value` has no final line ending, so a fenced code block whose only content is one blank line has an empty `value`, like an empty block. Raw HTML is a `html` node both as a block and inline; it's an HTML block when its parent is a block container (`root`, `blockquote`, `listItem` or `footnoteDefinition`) and inline HTML when its parent holds phrasing content. ```ts import { parse } from "@ende/markdown"; import { assertEquals } from "@ende/assert"; const ast = parse("See [the docs].\n\n[the docs]: https://docs.ende.sh"); assertEquals(ast.children.length, 1); assertEquals(ast.children[0], { type: "paragraph", children: [ { type: "text", value: "See " }, { type: "link", url: "https://docs.ende.sh", title: null, children: [{ type: "text", value: "the docs" }] }, { type: "text", value: "." } ] }); ``` ## GitHub Flavored Markdown The `gfm` option enables the extensions of the {@link https://github.github.com/gfm/ | GitHub Flavored Markdown Spec}, and footnotes: - Tables become `table`, `tableRow` and `tableCell` nodes, with the column alignments in `table.align`. - Task list items set `listItem.checked` to `true` or `false` (it's `null` for other items). - Strikethrough with one or two tildes (`~a~`, `~~a~~`) becomes `delete`. - Extended autolinks: `www.` addresses, `http://`, `https://` and `ftp://` URLs, and email addresses become `link` nodes without the `<` and `>`. - Footnotes: `[^label]: text` becomes a `footnoteDefinition`, which stays where it was written, and `[^label]` becomes a `footnoteReference`. Parsing and rendering match {@link https://github.com/github/cmark-gfm | cmark-gfm}, the implementation behind GitHub, and the extension examples of the GFM Spec and cmark-gfm's extension tests pass. `render()` writes footnotes the way GitHub does, with numbered references and a footnotes section at the end. Without `gfm`, parsing is pure CommonMark. ```ts import { parse, render } from "@ende/markdown"; import { assertEquals } from "@ende/assert"; const markdown = "| Feature | Done |\n| :-- | :-: |\n| Tables | ~~no~~ yes |\n"; assertEquals( render(parse(markdown, { gfm: true })), `
Feature Done
Tables no yes
` ); ``` GitHub's alerts are recognized as GitHub recognizes them: a block quote at the top level of the document (not inside a list, another block quote or a footnote) whose first line is just `[!NOTE]`, `[!TIP]`, `[!IMPORTANT]`, `[!WARNING]` or `[!CAUTION]`, in any case, with content after it. One extension: text after the marker on its line, such as `> [!TIP] Want to type-check only?`, is the alert's title, rendered in place of "Tip". jsDoc.doc:
Parses CommonMark into an mdast-shaped syntax tree. With the `gfm` option,
it also parses the GitHub Flavored Markdown extensions: tables, task list
items, strikethrough, extended autolinks, and footnotes, and GitHub's
alerts (`> [!NOTE]`), which become `admonition` nodes.

Every heading gets an `id` made from its plain text, by default as GitHub
makes it (see {@linkcode slug}), and unique within the document: a second
`Install` heading gets `install-1`.

Link reference definitions are resolved while parsing: reference links and
images become ordinary `link` and `image` nodes carrying
the definition's URL and title, and the definitions themselves don't appear
in the tree. Footnote definitions do stay in the tree.

Renders a syntax tree from `parse()` to HTML. The output matches the CommonMark reference implementation, commonmark.js, and for the GitHub Flavored Markdown nodes, cmark-gfm, with one difference by default: headings have an `id` attribute (their {@linkcode Heading.id}). The `headingIds: false` option turns that off. No id is written twice. Heading ids keep their values, since links and tables of contents use them; if a footnote's id (`fn-label`, `fnref-label`) is already taken by a heading or another footnote, the footnote's id gets a suffix (`fn-label-1`), and its links follow. Ids inside raw HTML aren't checked. An `admonition` renders as GitHub renders an alert, without the icon: a `
` holding a `

Note

` and the content. An admonition with a `title` has that title in place of the kind's name. Footnotes render as on GitHub: each `footnoteReference` becomes a numbered `` link, and the definitions that are referenced move into a `
` at the end, numbered in the order of their first reference, with links back to each reference. Definitions that are never referenced aren't rendered, and a reference without a definition renders as its source text.

jsDoc.doc:
Turns text into a heading id the way GitHub does (with the algorithm of
{@link https://github.com/Flet/github-slugger | github-slugger}): it
lowercases the text, removes everything except letters, marks, numbers,
connector punctuation such as `_`, hyphens and spaces, and turns each space
into a hyphen. Runs of spaces and hyphens aren't collapsed, and the result
isn't trimmed, so ids match GitHub's anchors.

This is the default `slugger` of `parse()`, which also makes the ids
unique; `slug()` alone doesn't. Character categories come from the
runtime's Unicode version, which can be newer than github-slugger's
(Unicode 13).

tags.name: text
tags.doc: The text to slug, such as a heading's plain text.
The slug, which can be empty.

jsDoc.doc:
Lists the headings of a document for a table of contents: each heading's
level, plain text and id, in document order. The list is flat; use
`depth` to indent or nest it. Headings inside block quotes, lists and
admonitions count too.

The `slug` is the heading's `id`, so it matches the `id` attribute
`render()` writes on the heading (unless the tree has duplicate ids, which
`parse()` never makes).

Calls `fn` for every node of the given type in a tree, in pre-order (a
parent before its children, children in document order), with the node's
index in its parent's `children` and the parent. For the node `visit()`
starts from, the index and parent are `null`.

`fn` may change the tree in two ways:

- Change the node itself, including replacing or editing its `children`:
  `visit()` reads `node.children` after `fn` returns, so it visits the new
  children.
- Replace the node, by assigning another node to `parent.children[index]`.
  The replacement isn't visited, nor are its children, so it can safely
  contain the original node (for example a link around inline code);
  `visit()` goes on with the next sibling.

Inserting or removing siblings (anything that changes the length of
`parent.children`) isn't supported: nodes can then be skipped or visited
twice.
